sources.project: cq-acis release metadata and pinned source
sources.observation: PyPI 0.3.12 was released 2026-10-16 with a trusted-publishing attestation to source commit e05a8f470d2f6799277f7b7df467d2fc35625889. The package is MIT, requires Python >=3.11 and CadQuery >=2.8, and publishes wheels for macOS ARM64, Windows x86-64, Linux x86-64, and Linux ARM64. The macOS ARM64 wheel SHA-256 is 94204f623d752e7dacf494bf631551277a985acbeb612ee3a24464ea0f0daab5. The project calls itself experimental and says its API/profile subset can change.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Published release identity and platform availability only; no package was installed or executed.
sources.planDisposition: Pin as an optional candidate for an isolated composed checkpoint; do not add it as a runtime or normal-test dependency.

sources.project: cq-acis SAT/SAB parser and geometry-conversion contracts
sources.observation: The project parses SAT/SAB into an ACIS model and converts a bounded subset to CadQuery/OpenCascade shapes. It documents analytic lines, circles, ellipses, planes, cylinders, cones, spheres, and tori, experimental explicit NURBS, selected tolerant boundaries, and restrictions on placements/trims/procedural geometry. It distinguishes the ACIS BinaryFile family from Autodesk ShapeManager ASM BinaryFile profiles and explicitly warns that version acceptance does not imply arbitrary-geometry support.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Source-level declared scope only; no execution against libdxfrw output or independently authored input occurred.
sources.planDisposition: Any result must be labeled by exact container, save version, record schema, geometry subset, and transform profile. Raw-byte retention and full semantic conversion remain separate.

sources.project: cq-acis source lineage, tests, and prior local witness
sources.observation: The SAB reader is described as written for cq-acis, with grammar/layout knowledge informed by cadmpeg (pinned Apache-2.0 Rust reference and CC-BY-4.0 format notes) and ezdxf (MIT); its public SAB fixtures also come from ezdxf. The separate parser converts through CadQuery/OpenCascade, the same kernel family as FreeCAD, not an independent geometry kernel. Tests assert analytic cube/prism metrics for ezdxf-authored inputs. Broader NIST corpus tests require valid, positive-volume shapes across 23 SAT artifacts / 147 bodies but do not establish independent expected geometry for each body. A prior local receipt records the already-run 5,489-byte scratch SAB 21800 witness as one valid solid/closed shell with expected bounds, about 385 volume, and area 334; it marks geometryObservationEligible=true but qualificationEligible=false because the witness was ezdxf-authored, the kernel is shared with FreeCAD, and no DWG/AcDs join was exercised.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Pinned source/test review in this pass plus a previously recorded single generated witness; this pass did not rerun it. Shared format-knowledge and fixture lineage prevent treating it as an independent layout vote or broad compatibility proof.
sources.planDisposition: Reuse the prior witness without rerunning. For any next semantic check, use locally generated input and expectations specified independently; do not count cq-acis as an independent-kernel vote or general producer-compatibility proof.

sources.observation: OCCT's standard open-source distribution provides the geometry/topology kernel; its ACIS SAT/SAB translator is listed among commercial components. cq-acis therefore supplies a distinct handwritten SAT/SAB parsing route to CadQuery/OCCT rather than wrapping a default open-source OCCT ACIS reader.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Official component catalog/announcement reviewed; no OCCT package was installed or inspected in a local build.
sources.planDisposition: Keep file parsing, geometry-kernel conversion, and native CAD consumer results separate. Do not attribute cq-acis output to an OCCT built-in ACIS translator.

sources.project: NIST Engineering Design Model corpus as optional cross-format lead
sources.observation: NIST describes a historical multi-format engineering-model repository. The cq-acis corpus pins NIST SAT inputs; some model folders have same-named VRML/display files. Same-name pairing does not prove identical revisions/geometries, tessellated display data is not an exact B-rep oracle, and NIST's license notice warns that third-party content may be present.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Repository metadata and publication only; no NIST drawing or display output was fetched, staged, or tested.
sources.planDisposition: Optional coarse bounds/shape comparison only after model pairing and licensing are checked. Do not import these samples into the libdxfrw repository; persistent fixtures must follow the existing from-scratch rule.

sources.observation: The 3DSOLID entity carries proprietary modeler data in groups 1/3 and an optional soft-owner history handle 350. 3DFACE stores WCS corner coordinates and invisible-edge flags. Polyface is a POLYLINE variant with vertex and face records, a four-vertex per-face limit, vertex-before-face writer ordering, and a reader tolerance requirement for unusual ordering.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Autodesk DXF schema documentation; no native AutoCAD acceptance or roundtrip was executed.
sources.planDisposition: Keep exact ACIS/modeler preservation and explicit mesh/facet conversion separate. Any faceted fallback must be declared lossy, counted, and source-linked.

sources.observation: The documented legacy DXF importer lists 3DFACE while the built-in importer list does not; neither documented backend currently reads embedded ACIS/SAT solids.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Consumer documentation only; no application/backend was run.
sources.planDisposition: Pin FreeCAD backend and per-entity result. Classify ACIS as unsupported by that consumer rather than a positive or negative parser verdict.

existingOwners: PAR-144 composed peer and compatibility checkpoint

implementationReadiness.defaultAction: Continue local dependency-ready implementation. Keep peer execution at the optional composed qualification checkpoint.
sequence: Use an isolated, exact-version cq-acis 0.3.12 runtime only after local fast checks; record platform wheel digest and runtime.

Reuse the already recorded simple scratch-box witness without rerunning it. If another geometry control is needed, author a non-rectangular asymmetric solid locally from scratch and specify its expected geometry independently; do not use shipped peer cube/prism as the sole pass case.

For DWG AcDs, use a separately pinned structural reader such as released ACadSharp v3.6.51 to establish section entry, schema/index decoding, raw SAB extraction, and owner/key/entity association before semantic conversion.
Pass exact recovered SAB bytes to cq-acis only for its documented profile; compare full body closure and independent analytic shape metrics, treating partial conversion as refusal.
Keep SAT/SAB parsing, AcDs structure, raw payload retention, attachment, DXF carrier, explicit facets, and native consumer acceptance as distinct matrix observations.
Do not copy external corpus files into this repository. A persistent test fixture must be locally created from scratch under the existing fixture policy.
If package/runtime/profile or exact AcDs input is missing, record NOT_EXERCISED and continue local implementation without waiting.

limitations: This pass was source, release-metadata, test-source, consumer-documentation, and repository-metadata research only; no package, peer executable, external sample, native app, or local test ran. The prior 0.3.12 local witness is recorded in deeper-broader-acis-peer-local-0_3_12-observation-2026-10-21.json and is not reasserted as newly run here.
cq-acis is experimental and its release/API/support matrix may change; pin exact package and digest for any future run.
Its disclosed SAB format-knowledge lineage includes cadmpeg and ezdxf; its geometry kernel path is useful only with independent expectations, not as a second independent file-layout vote.
cq-acis does not parse DWG AcDs sections or prove association of payloads to DWG entities.
ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 remains authoritative for DWG byte-layout questions.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting.
